name: Winning Their Place: Women Who Changed Sport
description: From the first Winter Games to Wimbledon and the Battle of the Sexes: the athletes who fought for the right to compete and changed what sport could be.

checkpoints.name: Closed doors
checkpoints.note: Lawn tennis, invented in 1873, is one of the first sports where women compete in public, and Wimbledon, begun in 1877, adds a women's event in 1884. No women take part in the Athens Games of 1896, but women first compete at the Paris Games of 1900, and at the first Winter Games in 1924 the figure skater Sonja Henie starts a career that makes her a star.

checkpoints.name: Olympic champions
checkpoints.note: At London in 1948 Fanny Blankers-Koen of the Netherlands wins four gold medals in athletics. The Soviet gymnast Larisa Latynina collects medals for years, and at Rome in 1960 Wilma Rudolph wins three sprint golds, the same year the first Paralympic Games are held in Rome.

checkpoints.name: Equal chances
checkpoints.note: Billie Jean King wins the Battle of the Sexes against Bobby Riggs in 1973 and campaigns for fair pay. In 1976 Nadia Comaneci scores the first perfect ten in Olympic gymnastics, and Martina Navratilova dominates Wimbledon.

checkpoints.name: Global stars
checkpoints.note: Serena Williams wins 23 Grand Slam singles titles, and Simone Biles reshapes gymnastics with moves no one had tried. At the London Games of 2012 women's boxing is added to the Olympic programme.
